items.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Prostikov was in the late ’70s. I missed a little period there. And he died in the ‘80s, in the early ‘80s. I went to Sophia. So I been taking piano for a long time

ctx.x: That was you in your forties, in the ‘70s.

And um, what’s his name – Prostikov was in the late ’70s. I missed a little period there. And he died in the ‘80s, in the early ‘80s. I went to Sophia. So I been taking piano for a long time, you know. When Sophia got sick, that’s what threw me off. So she got sick, and I got thrown off. I haven’t recovered yet, you know. But um, I always maintain that a cat should have a piano teacher. All of us. That’ll keep you working on something, you know. And it keeps you – keeps you occupied, ‘cause you have a lot of time…
At what point in your earlier life did you realize this is how you want to make a living – how was that process for you?
